originalTitle: France and Spain race to contain huge wildfires before fresh heatwave begins
summary: Coming days are ‘absolutely critical’ for firefighters before temperatures rise again this week, officials say
content: Firefighters in France and Spain are racing to bring huge wildfires under control before another heatwave this week that will complicate efforts to tame the flames. Spain’s interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, said Monday and Tuesday were “absolutely crucial days” before temperatures rise again from Wednesday. EU officials have said wildfires could still be burning until early November in what threatens to be a record-breaking year for the area of land burned. A fire in the hilly terrain of Ávila, west of Madrid, has become Spain’s largest on record, burning 50,000 hectares (125,000 acres). Authorities are battling two separate fires north-west of Madrid, taking the total area of scorched land near the capital to 70,000 hectares. France was also in “a race against time” to control wildfires before another heatwave this week, said Eric Brocardi, a fire service spokesperson. Weather forecasters have said temperatures could reach 40C (104F) is some parts of the country from Tuesday. This would complicate efforts to control the wildfire in Gironde in south-west France, which the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, described as “extremely intense and unpredictable … generating its own winds and advancing erratically toward the Bordeaux metropolitan area”. The French president, Emmanuel Macron, on a visit to Bordeaux, said: “The coming weeks will be tough and we have to hold out.” But he said a smaller fire in the adjoining Landes – which forced the evacuation of more than 30,000 people – was “contained” but remained “virulent”. “We must be extremely cautious over the next few hours and the coming days,” he said. The Gironde fire has so far burned 42,000 hectares, making it one of the biggest devastations of land in France since the second world war. In the Cestas commune, about 10 miles from the city of Bordeaux, firefighters used mechanical diggers to uproot trees in an attempt to create a firebreak. The vast fire, which has triggered the evacuation of 220,000 people, had not progressed during the early hours of Monday but was “not contained” and remained “very complicated to control”, Nuñez said. Speaking after an emergency meeting of the French government on Monday, he described this year’s wildfires as “completely exceptional”. More than 116,000 hectares of forest and vegetation have been burned since January, far exceeding the 70,000 hectares reported for the whole of 2025. Spain’s government said the 172,000 hectares of forested land burned this year was six times greater than the equivalent figure for 2025. The prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, told a climate conference the wildfires were not isolated incidents. “It is the most painful manifestation of a climate emergency that is making … wildfires more voracious and heatwaves more frequent, and as a result our land more vulnerable,” he said. “It is no longer an exception. It is the rule.” The European Commission’s lead official on the green transition, Teresa Ribera, said Europe was not prepared for the consequences of the climate crisis. In an interview with El País she said the commission would propose an adaptation strategy in October that would be much more comprehensive than policies implemented so far. A series of heatwaves, including record-breaking temperatures in June, that scientists say would have been impossible without the climate crisis, has left parched soils and tinder-dry vegetation that have fuelled this summer’s fires. A European Commission official said the wildfire season had begun in April and could last until early November. Officials also stressed the rising risks for fighting wildfires from the middle of the week in France, Spain and Greece. The EU executive has coordinated the dispatch of seven planes and four helicopters to France, as well as six planes and three forest firefighting teams to Spain, after the countries triggered the bloc’s emergency assistance mechanism. EU officials have also been sent to the Bordeaux region to assist local authorities. Officials stressed the unprecedented nature of recent fires, which have spread rapidly over large areas. A commission official said that a recent fire in southern Spain that killed 13 people had reached speeds of 4 mph, while firefighters are able to react only to fires moving 300 metres an hour or less. The scale of Europe’s wildfires has raised questions about the continent’s ability to respond. Italy is among about 10 European countries that have sent firefighting equipment or teams to France and Spain while grappling with its own blazes. Firefighters fought to extinguish a major wildfire in Italy’s southern region of Puglia on Monday. More than 400 people, many of them tourists staying in campsites set among pine forests, were evacuated by sea from the Gargano peninsula on Sunday as the blaze, fanned by strong winds, encroached on beaches. A further 58 people were evacuated from their homes in Maratea as a wildfire swept through neighbouring Basilicata. Italy is bracing for its fourth heatwave this year as temperatures edge up towards highs of 38C to 40C from Wednesday. Smoke from the fires in France is continuing to cause a “marked deterioration” in air quality across a swathe of the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region and beyond, with health authorities warning about the danger. Elderly people, pregnant women and those with respiratory issues and chronic conditions were advised to take precautions. Local health authorities said people should close windows, wear an FFP2 mask outside and avoid strenuous activity. The prime minister’s office said more than 1.5 million FFP2 masks had been sent to the region.
chineseTitle: 法国和西班牙在新的热浪开始之前竞相遏制巨大的野火
chineseSummary: 官员们表示，在本周气温再次上升之前，未来几天对消防员来说“绝对至关重要”
chineseContent: 法国和西班牙的消防队员正在加紧努力，在本周另一场热浪到来之前控制住巨大的野火，这将使扑灭大火的工作变得更加复杂。西班牙内政部长费尔南多·格兰德·马拉斯卡表示，周一和周二是“绝对关键的日子”，周三气温将再次上升。欧盟官员表示，野火可能会持续燃烧到11月初，今年被烧毁的土地面积可能会创纪录。马德里西部阿维拉丘陵地带的一场火灾已成为西班牙有记录以来最大的火灾，烧毁面积达 50,000 公顷（125,000 英亩）。当局正在扑灭马德里西北部的两场火灾，首都附近烧焦的土地总面积达到 70,000 公顷。消防部门发言人埃里克·布罗卡尔迪(Eric Brocardi)表示，法国也在“与时间赛跑”，以在本周另一场热浪到来之前控制野火。天气预报员表示，从周二开始，该国部分地区的气温可能达到 40 摄氏度（104 华氏度）。这将使控制法国西南部吉伦特省野火的工作变得更加复杂，内政部长洛朗·努涅斯(Laurent Nuñez)将野火描述为“极其强烈且不可预测……产生自己的风并不稳定地向波尔多大都市区推进”。法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙在访问波尔多时表示：“未来几周将很艰难，我们必须坚持下去。”但他表示，毗邻朗德省发生的一场规模较小的火灾，迫使三万多人疏散，虽然已得到“控制”，但仍然“严重”。 “在接下来的几个小时和未来几天里，我们必须极其谨慎，”他说。吉伦特省大火迄今已烧毁42,000公顷土地，成为二战以来法国最严重的土地破坏之一。在塞斯塔斯公社
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
